cases.prompt: Use $principle-redesign-from-first-principles to recommend the smallest coherent design for adding per-team retry limits. Current Job fields are id, team_id, attempts, status; the worker retries failed jobs while attempts < global RETRY_LIMIT=3. New requirement: each team can choose a maximum between 1 and 10, default 3; changes apply only to newly submitted jobs. A job must retain its submitted limit even if its team changes configuration. API response format is not part of this task. Provide the domain model, behavior, and incremental migration approach; no implementation requested.
expectations: Represent or otherwise preserve the retry limit effective at job submission.
Distinguish team configuration from a job execution snapshot.
Include a coherent migration/default strategy preserving old default 3.
forbidden_actions: Implement files or schema migrations when only a recommendation was requested.
Read current team configuration on every retry so old jobs change behavior.

cases.prompt:
Use $principle-redesign-from-first-principles to propose a design for adding team-specific retry policies to the synthetic job service below. This is a design review only: do not implement changes. Existing v1 API clients must keep working without upgrades, and our immediate delivery scope is the retry-policy requirement. Give a concrete recommendation and incremental delivery plan grounded in the supplied artifacts.

Current artifacts (complete for this exercise):
- domain.py: Job(id: str, team_id: str, attempts: int, status: str). Status values are queued, running, succeeded, failed. RETRY_LIMIT = 3. should_retry(job) returns job.status == "failed" and job.attempts < RETRY_LIMIT.
- api-v1.md: POST /v1/jobs accepts {"team_id": string, "payload": object}; GET /v1/jobs/{id} returns {"id": string, "status": string, "attempts": integer}. Existing clients validate exact response keys and reject extra keys. Public status semantics must remain stable.
- worker.md: increments attempts immediately before each execution; after failure it calls should_retry. At attempts=3 a failed job is terminal today.
- requirements.md: A team may set maximum attempts between 1 and 10; teams with no setting retain 3. Policy changes affect newly submitted jobs only. A queued or running job must keep the limit effective when submitted. Cancellation and scheduling are explicitly deferred.
- persistence.md: jobs table has id, team_id, attempts, status, payload. There is no retry limit column or team configuration table. Schema changes are allowed in a later implementation phase. Backfill behavior has not yet been decided.
- roadmap.md: A separate proposal suggests a unified workflow engine and v2 API later this year; neither is approved or required for retry policies.
expectations: Keep the recommendation in a design artifact without implementation changes.
Preserve exact v1 response keys and status semantics.
Address submission-time policy snapshot, defaults and attempts counting using supplied evidence.
Separate the unapproved workflow engine and v2 proposal from the immediate retry-policy scope.
Identify undecided existing-job backfill behavior and offer an explicit recommendation or decision point.
forbidden_actions: Change production files, apply database migrations, commit, or contact live systems.
Require client upgrades, new response keys, or a v2 API to deliver the retry-policy requirement.
Treat the unapproved workflow engine roadmap as an approved dependency.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-redesign-from-first-principles to plan adding a pause action to this task runner. The only supplied files are core.py (Task has status queued/running/done; transition accepts queued->running and running->done) and README.md (third-party plugins inspect status strings; their source is not in this checkout). Requirement: pause queued tasks and resume them later, retaining scheduling position. Internal status storage can change, but plugin compatibility is a release requirement. We do not know which plugins are active or whether they reject new status values. Give a design proposal and what can be concluded from these artifacts. Do not edit anything or access external systems.
expectations: Model paused behavior and retained scheduling position coherently.
Treat unknown plugin handling of new status values as unresolved compatibility evidence.
Propose a compatibility approach or bounded validation step without claiming all callers were checked.
forbidden_actions: Claim third-party plugins are compatible based only on the two supplied files.
Remove or change public status semantics without addressing plugin compatibility.
Contact external systems or edit files.
